details: taste: core-tests-not-in-gate (23 Oct). Tests that read committed text (committed_items, committed_text in tests/test_queue.py) see the old commit while a worker loops on uncommitted edits, so `bin/ci --quick` is green in the worktree and the gate on the commit is red; one ~8 min gate run and a fixer round were spent on it. It repeats on every change that touches a file such a test reads.
failing_case: On wt/core-tests-not-in-gate, bin/ci with the edit uncommitted: green; the same edit committed: TestSeedItems.test_f14_a_where_line_names_the_line_the_item_talks_about fails ('*inject-addition*' not found).
pass_cases: An edit that breaks a committed-text test fails `bin/ci --quick` before the commit as it does after it, or the run states it checked HEAD only.
reason: tests/test_quick_head.py:10 passes with the fix and fails at 57cc76f; it asserts an uncommitted edit is read. Gate cf7ee23 exit 0, no file after it.
findings.summary: The quick check passes before a commit and fails after

details: CONFIRMED by reading: git() in tests/test_queue.py:24-28 returns done.stdout.strip(); committed_text (line 375) and
committed_items (line 369) add "\n" to it in the probe path, while the tree path (lines 368, 376) returns the file
exactly. Today README and every item end in exactly one newline with no leading space, so nothing fails: fragile, LOW.
evidence: tail -c 50 .relay/README.md | od -c  ->  ... c o m m i t t e d . \n   (one newline today)
failing_case: relay_setup.RELAY_README and .relay/README.md both end "...never committed.\n\n" (or both lack the last newline).
Outer gate run: committed_text reads the tree exactly, equal, test_f14_setups_readme_text_is_relays_own_readme passes.
Nested inert-probe run: committed_text reads `git show HEAD^:...` through git(), which strips, then adds "\n": "...\n" is
not equal, the test fails. The gate goes red only at "inert" with "a step's result or the test count changed when only
inert files changed", pointing at inert files when nothing inert is at fault. Before this change both runs read through
git() and agreed. Same for a queue item in committed_items (round-trip test).
fix_hint: Read the probe path raw: subprocess git show without strip (or a git(..., strip=False)), so both paths return the file's
exact bytes; or normalise the tree path the same way. One small test: a file ending "\n\n" reads the same in both paths.
pass_cases: - README and RELAY_README identical, ending in one newline: outer and probe runs both pass (today's case).
- README and RELAY_README identical, ending "\n\n": outer and probe runs give the same result (both pass, or both fail).
- An item with an uncommitted appended line, no probe commit: committed_items returns the text with the line (test_q1_an_uncommitted_edit...).
- A probe commit appending "inert probe line": committed_items and committed_text return the text of HEAD^ (test_q1_a_probe_commit...).
reason: tests/test_quick_head.py:31 (test_f1) passes; fails at 57cc76f. Helpers now use show_raw, byte-exact in both paths (tests/test_queue.py:354-383).
findings.summary: outer run reads inert text byte-exact from the tree, the probe run reads it from git stripped plus one newline: the two runs can now disagree
